audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart handed Levels 1-5 to Irelia and Levels 6+ to 'Skill', which is the exact inverse of both the packet levelChart and the content-layer win[] row, and it contradicted its own phases[].why text (rows 0-3 describe Malzahar shoving comfortably).
audit.why: Irelia has no ranged pressure and 15-mana Bladesurge only threatens once she has a Marked target or a reset; Malzahar shoves the first four levels with Malefic Visions. Her spike is 6 (Vanguard's Edge plus a Flawless Duet stun cancelling the Nether Grasp channel) through first item.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 = Skill (even), rows 4-5 = Irelia, row 6 = Skill. Content win[] already reads this way, so only the full layer moves.

audit.why: Spikes as written are accurate: Irelia's level 6 (Vanguard's Edge, 125/105/85s) plus Trinity/Bork is her window; Malzahar returns to even with Zhonya's answering the post-stun follow-up. Recorded, and the phases[4]/[5] why lines were rewritten to state the same shift now that the side flags agree.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[5].why now name Vanguard's Edge and the Flawless Duet channel-cancel as the reason those rows belong to Irelia.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns cited a fabricated Malzahar passive named 'Iron Boundary' and contained no cooldown number at all. The decisive interaction — Flawless Duet's stun cancelling the Nether Grasp channel — was never stated as an interaction, only alluded to.
audit.why: Malzahar's passive is Void Shift. His R is flagged channel: 'interruptible — any CC cancels it', and Irelia's E is flagged hardCC. That single interaction decides the matchup and belongs in the cooldowns field with real numbers: Flawless Duet 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Bladesurge 10/9/8/7/6s with a reset on Marked or dying targets, Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85s, Nether Grasp 140/110/80s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the four real cooldowns and the channel-cancel stated outright; 'Iron Boundary' removed everywhere it appeared.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bladesurge's heal was never answered with a Grievous Wounds timing anywhere in the prose.
audit.why: Brief missingInteractions rule needs-antiheal: Irelia sustains through chip damage via Bladesurge, so anti-heal timing decides extended trades — and Malefic Visions is pure chip damage.
audit.corrected: Folded into 'ahead': buy anti-heal against Bladesurge sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Vanguard's Edge creates terrain that cuts a dashless champion's retreat.
audit.why: Brief missingInteractions rule terrain-cuts-retreat: Irelia's R (950 range, terrain flag) walls off the escape and Malzahar owns no dash, so Flash is a wall answer here, not a damage answer.
audit.corrected: Folded into breakdown.mid and dontsFull[2] context.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twenty lint findings: sixteen misgendered fields calling Irelia he/his/him, two copy-paste bleeds (dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim), one unsupported magnitude ('TP doubles your...'), one cooldowns field with no digit.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists irelia as female; the bled bullets promised one thing in the title and explained another in the body.
audit.corrected: All twenty fixed in the edits below; bled bodies replaced with content that matches their titles.

notes: Level chart: the FULL layer was inverted against both packet.levelChart and content win[], and against its own why text. Content win[] already matched the packet, so per the chart rule only the full layer's side/rating/why moved and no win[N] edits were proposed (they would be no-ops). Rating scale read as difficulty-for-you (7/10 = her window), consistent with diffRating 7/10. 'Iron Boundary' is a fabricated name for Malzahar's passive — the real name is Void Shift (damage reduction + CC immunity, not a spell shield); removed from breakdown.cooldowns and reworded in report[8] and loading. Fields judged templated but left alone for lack of anything Irelia-specific to ground them in: breakdown.early, breakdown.late, breakdown.spikes, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d. Content layer needed no edits — spikes[0..3], early/mid/late and wants[] are already Irelia-specific and factually correct.
